newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Tourism Authority calls for black empowerment.
newsitem.headline: Tourism Authority calls for black empowerment.

text.p: The Zimbabwe Tourism Authority should implement the government's black empowerment policy to ensure the whole country benefits, a cabinet minister told a tourism conference on Monday.

Addressing the Tourism International Investment Conference in Harare, Environment and Tourism Minister Chen Chimutengwende said tourism needed to be diversified away from select sites like the Victoria Falls.
"The tourism sector is the fastest growing sector in our economy. We need to diversify our product and ensure the whole country can benefit. More players must be involved," he said.
"The ZTA (Zimbabwe Tourism Authority) should ensure that the government's policy of indigenisation (black empowerment) is also implemented in the tourism sector."
President Robert Mugabe said last year that tourism had grown at an average rate of 10 percent a year since Zimbabwe's independence from Britain in 1980.
The industry netted about Z$2 billion (US$182 million) in 1996, a five percent increase on the previous year.
